subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Pillars of Creation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Pillars of Creation.

hook.text: Hubble's most famous image shows towering columns of gas where new stars are forming. They're called the Pillars of Creation.

buildup.text: The pillars sit inside the Eagle Nebula, 6,500 light-years away. Each tower is several light-years tall.

discovery.text: Ultraviolet radiation from nearby hot stars is slowly eroding the pillars, sculpting them into their shapes.

twist.text: The pillars may already be gone. A supernova blast likely destroyed them 6,000 years ago—the light just hasn't reached us.

climax.text: James Webb re-imaged the Pillars in infrared, revealing newborn stars glowing inside the dust columns.

punchline.text: Six-thousand-year-old light. The pillars may already be gone.

quiz.question: Why might the Pillars of Creation no longer exist?
options: A nearby supernova may have destroyed them, but the light hasn't reached us yet
They naturally evaporate after a few million years
The stars inside them consumed all the gas

details.summary: The Pillars of Creation are towering columns of gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula, famously photographed by Hubble in 1995. These light-year-tall structures are being sculpted by radiation from nearby hot stars while simultaneously birthing new stars within their dense tips — creation and…
details.whyItMatters: The Pillars of Creation became the most iconic astronomical image ever taken, showing the public that star birth is a dramatic, beautiful process. The James Webb Space Telescope later revealed even more detail in infrared light.
takeaways: They're towering gas columns in the Eagle Nebula
Radiation sculpts them while new stars form inside
Hubble's 1995 image became astronomy's most iconic photograph

faq.question: Are the Pillars of Creation still there?
faq.answer: Possibly not. A 2007 Spitzer Space Telescope observation suggested a supernova shockwave may have already destroyed them about 6,000 years ago. Since the Eagle Nebula is 6,500 light-years away, we won't see the destruction for another 1,000 years.

faq.question: How tall are the Pillars of Creation?
faq.answer: The tallest pillar stretches about 4-5 light-years from base to tip — roughly the distance from the Sun to the nearest star. Despite looking delicate, each pillar contains enough gas and dust to form thousands of stars. Their beauty masks enormous scale.
